description: Tar the small-and-precious set (XMPs, .scouter/, config, metrics.db, events.jsonl), hash and encrypt it (age if configured, else openssl enc), rsync the raws, write a manifest, and prune old archives beyond keep_archives (never the newest two). Refuses when the backup gate is not satisfied. Requires confirm=true: it writes outside the library and deletes old archives.

confirm.description: required: writes outside the library and prunes old archives

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

name: backup_run

description: Decrypt the newest archive (or --archive TS) to a temp directory, compare the ciphertext and plaintext sha256 against the manifest, re-hash a sample of members and of the rsynced raws. Read-only; writes nothing outside its own temp directory.
name: backup_verify

description: Write the starter Scouter config file (~/.config/scouter/config.json by default). backup.enabled is false in the starter file, so the first import fails loudly until a target is set. Requires confirm=true to write, or to replace an existing file.

confirm.description: required to write, or to replace an existing file

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

name: config_init

description: Show the loaded Scouter config and whether the backup gate currently passes -- the one call that answers 'will an import work right now?' without attempting one.
name: config_show

description: Apply a cull.propose proposal's ratings via the image.rate bridge verb, in batches of 50, verified by polling each changed frame's XMP sidecar. Refuses (usage) if any frame's sidecar changed since the proposal was written. Requires confirm=true: a cull touches many images.

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

job_slug.description: job slug; loads the newest cull-*.json unless proposal is given

name: cull_apply

description: Propose a rating for every frame in a job (or an explicit image list), grouped into bursts by capture time and camera. Never proposes rating 0 or reject -- stats cannot see eyes, expression or a deliberate motion blur, so a flagged frame gets rating 1 with its numbers and the human decides. Every reason names the numbers behind it. Read-only: writes no rating and calls the bridge only for the read-only image.lookup behind image resolution.

images.description: explicit image list, instead of (or alongside) --job-slug

items.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

job_slug.description: job slug; frames come from its import.json

name: cull_propose

description: The darkroom image's committed history: every module, whether it is active, and its decoded parameters where a verified layout exists (otherwise opaque hex plus the module version).

image.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

name: darkroom_describe_history

description: Enable a module on the darkroom image.

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

name: darkroom_enable

description: Move a slider by darktable's own default step, up (positive steps) or down (negative). Use when the user says 'a bit more'.

commit.description: commit history to the XMP after the write

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

name: darkroom_nudge

description: Load an image in darktable's darkroom view, importing it into the library first if it is not there. Every other darkroom tool needs this first: slider actions only work in the darkroom.

image.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

name: darkroom_open

description: Reset a module to its defaults. DESTRUCTIVE: the module's parameters are discarded and Scouter cannot undo it (only the user's own Ctrl-Z can). Requires confirm=true; without it you get the plan and nothing happens.

confirm.description: required: authorises discarding this module's parameters

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

name: darkroom_reset

description: Set one module parameter to an absolute value on the image currently open in the darkroom. Creates one darktable history item the user can see and undo. Values are read back from the XMP sidecar after the commit.

commit.description: commit history to the XMP after the write

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

module.description: darktable module, e.g. exposure, sigmoid, temperature, colorbalancergb

value.description: absolute value in the slider's own unit (EV for exposure, K for temperature)

name: darkroom_set

description: Current view plus normalised slider POSITIONS (0..1). These are positions, not parameter values: use history_read for values.
name: darkroom_status

description: Revert the newest Scouter write in this job by setting the parameter back to its previous value. This adds a new history item rather than deleting one, so the user's own undo still works.

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

name: darkroom_undo_last

description: Export a job's selected frames through a preset, with a checksum manifest. Selection is --images if given, else every raw in import.json whose rating >= min_rating (client-proof/preview) or that carries the configured colour label (client-final/print-tiff). Requires confirm=true to overwrite an existing preset output.

confirm.description: required to overwrite an existing preset output

date.description: disambiguate when the slug matches more than one job

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

images.description: explicit image list, overriding the selection rule

items.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

style.description: apply this style at render time only; nothing in the library changes

name: export_release

description: Export images through a preset. client-final is a full-size sRGB JPEG; preview is a 1024 px PNG. Requires confirm=true for more than one image or to overwrite an existing file.

confirm.description: required for n>1 images or to overwrite files

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

items.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

name: export_run

description: Re-hash a release manifest's outputs against it. The manifest's own .sha256 sidecar is required, not optional -- a missing sidecar is manifest_unauthenticated. Read-only.

manifest.description: path to a manifest-<preset>-<ts>.json written by export.release

root.description: directory files[].output resolves against; default is the manifest's own <job>/.scouter/ parent. Pass this to verify a manifest shipped beside its exports/ folder instead

name: export_verify

description: Whether an image's XMP sidecar is still the one Scouter last committed (a watermark comparison, not a bounce). A pure read: no darkroom action, no history.commit. Call this before a repeat set to skip a bounce it already knows will find nothing to write.

image.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

name: history_changed

description: Make darktable write the darkroom image's history to its XMP sidecar, then verify the file actually changed. darktable only commits when the darkroom is left, so this is what makes an edit readable.

attempts.description: view-bounce attempts, clamped to 1..3; a caller sure this is a no-op should pass 1

expect_change.description: False forces attempts=1 and reports a confirmed no-op as ok/changed=false instead of raising commit_timeout

image.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

strategy.description: commit trigger; auto picks the cheapest that works on this build

timeout_s.description: seconds to wait for the sidecar to change

name: history_commit

description: Read an image's history from its XMP sidecar. Returns confirmed=false when the sidecar is missing or mid-write.

image.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

name: history_read

description: Copy, checksum, rename and register a memory card into the library. Refuses with backup_not_configured before reading a single file unless the backup gate passes (config.show reports its verdict). Always requires confirm=true: an import is always more than one file. Originals are copied read-only (chmod 0444) and verified with two independent sha256 passes; a darktable that is not running does not fail the import (film_roll_registered: false, retry with library.register).

camera.description: camera slug override; required for a mixed-camera card

confirm.description: required: an import always touches more than one file

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD; default: the earliest capture time

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

name: library_import

description: List every job under the library root: frame count, bytes, a ratings histogram from the XMPs' xmp:Rating, and which .scouter manifests exist. Read-only.
name: library_jobs

description: Re-register a job's film roll with darktable (e.g. after importing with darktable closed). Requires confirm=true: it writes to darktable's own library.

date.description: disambiguate when the slug matches more than one job

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

name: library_register

description: Move the library to a new root: rewrite library_root in the config (every other key survives untouched) and re-verify every job's checksums there. Requires confirm=true: it rewrites the config file and its dry run reports which jobs already exist at the new root. Never edits darktable's library.db -- darktable's film rolls keep pointing at the old paths, so re-import <new_root>/<job>/raw for each job afterwards (the result's next_step says so).

confirm.description: required: rewrites the config and writes outside the library

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

name: library_relocate

description: Re-hash raw/ against the job's .scouter/checksums.sha256 manifest. Read-only. `.xmp` sidecars are excluded by suffix, not by silence.

date.description: disambiguate when the slug matches more than one job

name: library_verify

description: Per-verb calls, error rate by class, p50/p95 latency and estimated tokens over a time window.
name: metrics_summary

description: Flag frames whose rendered exposure, white balance or clipping drift too far from the reference (hero) frame -- ev_proxy vs tolerances.exposure_ev, Kelvin (or, with no calibration table, the wb_ratio_rg/bg fallback) vs tolerances.temperature_k / wb_ratio, and clipped_high_pct vs tolerances.clipped_high_pct. Read-only: one metrics event, scout.stats_many and the XMP sidecars only, no bridge writes. The reference is excluded from its own comparison. A frame whose stats failed to render is reported in `failed`, never counted as within tolerance.

images.description: explicit image list, instead of (or alongside) job_slug (the reference is excluded from its own comparison either way)

items.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

job_slug.description: job slug; frames come from its import.json

reference.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

name: outliers_list

description: Numeric distance between two images' current renders (deltas are b minus a).

a.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

b.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

budget_s.description: loop budget; over it, re-render at 512 px

px.description: longest edge of the render in pixels

name: scout_compare

description: Render a viewable preview and return its FILE PATH. The pixels are never inlined; read the file at preview_path yourself.

image.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

px.description: longest edge of the render in pixels

name: scout_preview

description: Render the image at N px through darktable-cli and return the per-channel histogram, clipping percentages, luminance percentiles, white-balance ratios and a sharpness score. Statistics are 8-bit and the luminance histogram is an estimate.

budget_s.description: loop budget; over it, re-render at 512 px

image.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

px.description: longest edge of the render in pixels

name: scout_stats

description: Apply a style to ONE image (applying to a set is phase 2). mode=append adds to the history; mode=overwrite is refused with unsupported_mode, because darktable's Lua API cannot replace history.

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

image.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

mode.description: append adds to history; overwrite is refused (unsupported_mode), never silently downgraded to append

name: style_apply

description: Apply one style to a whole set, batched through the bridge, keeping per-image results. Always requires confirm=true (a set apply is always a bulk write). outcome=partial (exit 9) when some images applied and some did not, or any id came back unknown (a bridge timeout, or an unconfirmed sidecar the idempotency guard could not verify) -- the successes are kept, never discarded. A target Scouter's own ledger (job/.scouter/styles-applied.json) says already carries this style is skipped by default (image:apply_style always appends, so re-applying would stack a second copy); force=true applies anyway. mode=overwrite is refused with unsupported_mode; the only place overwrite exists at all is the render-only `export.release --overwrite-style`.

batch.description: how many image ids per bridge call

confirm.description: required: applying to a set is always gated

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

exclude.description: paths or image ids to leave out of the set

items.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

force.description: apply even to images Scouter's own ledger says already carry this style (job/.scouter/styles-applied.json)

images.description: paths or image ids; defaults to every file in job_slug's import.json

items.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

job_slug.description: job whose import.json lists the set (used when images is not given)

mode.description: append adds to history; overwrite is refused (unsupported_mode)

name: style_apply_set

description: Save the image's history as a darktable style, filtered to `modules` by writing a .dtstyle from the XMP (no darkroom needed). `no_filter=true` also reads the sidecar and requires a committed history: it ignores `modules` as a restriction and keeps every active operation instead (native darkroom path when nothing is forbidden), but still excludes cfg.style.never_include -- crop, retouch, spot white balance, ... -- either way. `modules` naming a forbidden op is always refused, even with no_filter=true -- an explicit request wins over no_filter's 'ignore modules' meaning. Requires confirm=true when a style of that name already exists.

confirm.description: required to replace an existing style

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

image.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

modules.description: modules to keep -- filtered for real by default

no_filter.description: reads the sidecar and requires a committed history, same as the default path; ignores `modules` and keeps every active operation instead (never_include is still excluded either way -- naming a forbidden op in `modules` is still refused)

name: style_extract

description: The conversational vocabulary: every module parameter Scouter can move by words, with unit, safe range, step, and status (live, absolute_only, candidate, unreachable). Read once per session.

module.description: only this module's rows, e.g. colorbalancergb

name: vocab_list

description: Sweep the darkroom's Kelvin slider from k_from to k_to and write the measured per-camera table `~/.config/scouter/wb/<camera>.json`, which wb.kelvin and outliers.list's temperature_k_delta then use. Costs ~1.8s per point and adds one history item per point, so it refuses inside a job's raw/ unless allow_in_job=true -- run it on a scratch copy. Refuses (usage error) rather than write a table whose r/b coefficient ratio is not strictly increasing in Kelvin. Requires confirm=true to run at all (never overwrites an existing table otherwise).

allow_in_job.description: required: image is inside a job's raw/

confirm.description: required to run at all (never overwrites without it)

dry_run.description: plan only: return what would happen and send nothing

image.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

name: wb_calibrate

description: Invert an image's committed `temperature` coefficients to Kelvin against its camera's measured calibration table (scouter wb calibrate). No table -> kelvin: null, reason names `scouter wb calibrate`. Outside the calibrated range -> kelvin: null, reason names the range -- never an extrapolated guess.

image.description: absolute path to the raw file, or a darktable image id

name: wb_kelvin
